project.name: Tokenization Platform
project.purpose: Self-hosted, permissioned, closed-loop real-world-asset tokenization platform, real-estate first, settling in Iranian Rial on an internal ledger
project.regulatory_posture: asserts no compliance; jurisdiction rules are configuration marked REQUIRES LOCAL LEGAL VALIDATION

architecture.backend: NestJS 11 on Express, TypeScript strict + exactOptionalPropertyTypes + noUncheckedIndexedAccess
architecture.frontend: Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, zero UI dependencies, hand-rolled design system
architecture.chain: EVM (anvil devnet), ERC-3643 (T-REX) + ONCHAINID, ethers v6
architecture.multi_tenancy: tenant_id everywhere; AsyncLocalStorage TenantContext; Prisma Proxy that forbids findUnique/update/upsert/delete
architecture.auth: jose JWT in httpOnly cookie or Bearer (cookie wins); argon2; TOTP MFA opt-in for officers; deny-by-default RBAC

risks.title: Single hot key controls mint/burn/claims and derives custodial wallets
KYC evidence encryption key is a plain env var with no rotation or escrow
No retention or erasure policy for personal data
Chain writes are synchronous and unrecoverable
Ledger is single-entry with no conservation invariants
Rate limiting is in-memory per process

current_milestone.name: Sanctions & PEP screening — a mock that cannot lie about itself
current_milestone.state: Shipped and verified in a browser: an officer can screen an applicant and reads the outcome with a SIMULATED disclaimer beside it; an applicant with no declared name is refused with 409 and a readable reason. The adapter checks nothing and says so — simulated: true is hard-coded in the mock, and the disclaimer lives in the result, not in a log line. Results are append-only. Choosing a real provider remains an owner decision (OD-11). Risk rating now ships alongside it: an officer rates an applicant against a PROVISIONAL model (REQUIRES LOCAL LEGAL VALIDATION, shown on the card), the rating is advisory and decides nothing, and an unrated file reads as unrated rather than low. Periodic review scheduling — the third part of the roadmap's 4.2 line — is NOT built. Periodic review scheduling now completes the roadmap's 4.2 line: approved customers whose review has lapsed appear on their own screen, worst first, with never-reviewed ranked ahead of overdue. The cadence is provisional and shown as such. No scheduler runs and nothing is restricted — it is a work list.

open_questions_for_owner: Concrete field list an issuer may see about investors
Block asset approval until the rights matrix is established?
OD-23 mandatory MFA for privileged roles?
Queue semantics for applications waiting on the applicant
Should a KYC-rejected applicant be able to re-apply?
Should draft offerings be visible to signed-in investors?
K-27 remainder: the 20/min credential budget is per-IP, so a CGNAT population shares one login budget (K-9). Per-account throttling, a shared store, or accept-for-pilot?
4.2: which real sanctions/PEP provider (if any) should replace the mock? Until one is chosen the platform screens nobody, and every result is labelled SIMULATED in the officer's view.

3.3 exit criterion, still unmet: how much of the asset submission wizard should exist (drafts, completeness, validation, review comments, status history)? A scope call, not an engineering one — carried forward from the 3.3 milestone.

4.2 risk model: the factors and weights in `application/risk/risk-model.ts` are a generic placeholder I wrote, NOT a methodology. Which factors, which weights, and where the medium/high thresholds sit are compliance-policy inputs — replace them before any production use.

4.2 periodic review: how often must a customer be re-screened and re-rated (commonly risk-driven: e.g. high annually, low every few years)? The cadence is a policy input; the scheduling machinery is not built and is the remaining part of roadmap 4.2.
4.2 review cadence: high 12 / medium 24 / low 36 months is a placeholder shape (higher band reviewed more often), not a policy. Confirm or replace in `application/risk/risk-model.ts`.

4.2 periodic review: should a lapsed review DO anything beyond appearing on the list — a reminder to the officer, or a restriction on the customer? Today it does neither, deliberately; a restriction is a compliance-policy decision and a reminder needs an audience (the pg-boss scanner precedent used 'staff holding the permission').

4.2: should the periodic-review list join the ops work queue? Its contents (pending KYC + approvals + redemptions) were YOUR decision on 2026-07-28, so I built this as its own screen rather than widening that queue.
